item.title: Breaking: Two suspected Ebola cases identified in North-East Nigeria – NCDC
item.description: Two suspected cases of Ebola disease have been identified in Nigeria’s North-East region, with both individuals isolated as health authorities conduct investigations and laboratory tests. An update on the disease situation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), said contact identification and listing were ongoing, while samples from the suspected cases were being subjected to laboratory testing. It clarified that the classification of the individuals as suspected cases did not mean they had tested positive for Ebola, noting that confirmation would depend on laboratory results. The public was advised to maintain proper hand hygiene, practise enhanced sanitation and follow preventive guidance issued by public health authorities. The update added that further information would be provided as verified details become available. item.title: ADC-PCC gives Sokoto authorities 24-hr ultimatum over attack on guber candidate
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has given security authorities in Sokoto State 24 hours to arrest those behind an attack on its governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya. The ultimatum followed the alleged attack by operatives of the state-owned Sokoto Marshals, the vandalisation of several vehicles in the candidate’s convoy and the reported abduction of two Department of State Services (DSS) personnel attached to him. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said the attack occurred along Airport Road, Sokoto, on Friday night, as Dan Iya returned to the city after accompanying former governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, from the airport. Ologbondiyan said the candidate’s personal SUV was among the vehicles vandalised, adding that Dan Iya had personally reported the incident to the Sokoto State Commissioner of Police. But the council said the attack was only part of a wider campaign of intimidation, alleging that operatives of the Sokoto Marshals had taken positions at various historic gates into the metropolis, harassing motorists and targeting vehicles displaying ADC posters, insignia and other party symbols. It said the reported abduction of two DSS personnel attached to the candidate had further heightened concerns over the incident. “This is not governance. It is banditry in uniform, and it must not be tolerated in a democracy,” Ologbondiyan declared. The ADC-PCC described the incident as part of what it called a growing pattern of political violence against opposition figures, recalling similar attacks reportedly recorded in Kaduna and other states in recent weeks. It warned that the party would no longer stand by while its candidates, leaders and members were subjected to intimidation and violence, insisting that it was prepared to defend their constitutional rights through every legitimate means. The council called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Sokoto Commissioner of Police and relevant security and intelligence agencies to immediately investigate the attack, arrest those responsible and secure the release of the two DSS personnel. It gave the authorities 24 hours to rein in the operatives, guarantee the safety of its candidate and members, and commence decisive action against those implicated. “Failure to do so will leave the leadership of our party with no option but to take further decisive and lawful steps to protect its members, defend its political rights and safeguard our democracy,” the statement warned. The ADC-PCC cautioned that the alleged deployment of a taxpayer-funded security outfit against political opponents could push the country towards an era of state-backed political intimidation, insisting that it would resist any attempt to silence the opposition through violence. item.title: Atiku’s son: ‘My support for Tinubu is personal’; pledges 10 buses
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA The son of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Abba, has said his decision to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election is a personal choice made in conscience, which he acknowledged may be viewed against the political positions of people he shares family relationships with. Read Also: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain Abubakar, Founder and Chairman of the Haske Bola Tinubu Organisation, HBTO, made the declaration at the group’s press conference in Abuja. He said political decisions that differ from the positions of relatives “often attract considerable public attention” and that he was “equally conscious that my own political decision may be viewed within this context.” “However, I wish to make one fundamental point: political conviction is a matter of personal judgement, conscience and the freedom of every individual to make independent choices,” he said. He described the formation of HBTO as “a deliberate political choice, one I have made in my personal capacity and with a firm belief in the direction we have chosen to pursue. “I hold no reservations about the right of others to their differing political opinions, just as I expect my own convictions to be respected,” he added. Abba Abubakar said HBTO is a political mobilisation and support platform established to bring together Nigerians who share a common conviction in the leadership and reform agenda of the president and the All Progressives Congress, APC-led administration. item.title: CAN questions conviction of Christian woman in Borno
item.description: …Raises religious freedom concerns By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has faulted the reported conviction and imprisonment of a Christian woman in Borno State, raising concerns over religious freedom and the protection of fundamental rights. The woman, identified in circulating reports as Lami Samuel Dawa, was reportedly convicted in a case said to have involved the conversion of an adult woman to Christianity. CAN said the precise facts and legal basis of the conviction were still being verified. In a statement by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the association disclosed that an appeal had been filed, adding that it was committed to allowing the judicial process to run its course. “The Association believes that every individual has the right to freely choose, change or practise their religion or belief without coercion, intimidation or unlawful punishment,” CAN said. The association urged the relevant authorities to protect the rights of all parties and ensure that justice was served in accordance with the Constitution and the law. CAN also pledged to monitor developments and engage the authorities through appropriate legal and institutional channels, while reaffirming its commitment to peaceful coexistence among Nigerians of different religious backgrounds. It said the case highlighted the need to protect the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed to every citizen, including the right to freely choose and practise a religion. item.title: 2027 elections fixed, can’t be shifted – Amupitan
item.description: …says INEC would pay special attention to Rivers By Davies Iheamnachor PORT HARCOURT: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has stressed that the commission would not alter the timetable for the 2027 general elections, insisting that the elections must hold as already scheduled. Amupitan stated this during the commission’s interactive meeting with staff members of the Commission in all six states of South-South geopolitical zone and assessment of their readiness for the 2027 general elections, which held in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing participants, Amupitan said the commission’s statutory timeline for the elections was fixed and would not be adjusted for no reason, noting that INEC was committed to delivering credible elections in line with the provisions of the law. He said: “Our statutory timeline is fixed. We will not change anything. The election must hold as scheduled.” The INEC boss also disclosed that Rivers State would receive special attention from the commission in the elections, following its position as the state with the highest number of registered voters in the South-South region. He outlined that Rivers had 3,736,434 registered voters, followed by Delta State with 3,525,988; Edo, 2,865,263; Akwa Ibom, 2,566,198; Cross River, 1,928,978; and Bayelsa, 1,200,691. Amupitan notrd that the six states have a total of 15,823,550 registered voters, adding that the electoral would pay closer attention to Rivers because of its electoral significance in the region. He said: “With the 3,736,434 registered voters for Rivers State, the state leads the South-South. By this, the commission will put more attention to what happens in Rivers State. It is your duty to ensure that no voter is disenfranchised because of operational failures.” Amupitan disclosed that INEC had published the voters’ register online and at designated locations, adding that it had received over 5,000 claims relating to corrections including names and date of birth and more than 600 objections, which were being addressed to ensure a credible voter register ahead of the elections. He further announced that the final voters’ register would be released on December 15, saying the commission was committed to resolving all outstanding issues before the deadline. The INEC chairman, who explained that he had initially considered revalidating the voters’ register upon assuming office, said the idea was dropped following concerns that the exercise would be too close to the general elections. He also expressed confidence in the commission’s capacity to conduct peaceful, transparent and credible elections, citing lessons learnt from recent off-cycle governorship elections, particularly the Osun State election. Amupitan noted that the Osun election recorded the highest voter turnout in the history of off-cycle elections in the state and was adjudged locally and internationally as credible despite earlier security concerns. item.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against pundit Carragher
item.description: Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against former Liverpool defender-turned-pundit Jamie Carragher for what the club described as “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters. Carragher, a prominent pundit with Sky Sports and CBS, has been hit with a backlash by Villa fans for suggesting that manager Unai Emery should be a candidate to replace the under-fire Michael Carrick at Manchester United. “Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris said in a short statement posted on the club’s social media feeds. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football.” Emery has transformed Villa’s fortunes since taking charge four years ago. The Spaniard has led the Birmingham-based club twice into the Champions League and ended a 30-year wait for silverware by winning the Europa League last season. However, he has had to build a new team this season after six of the side that started the Europa League final departed in the transfer market, seeking either higher wages or the chance to challenge more routinely for silverware. Emery also enjoyed success at Valencia and Sevilla, but struggled with higher demands in spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. “Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” Carragher told the Stick to Football podcast. “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.” AFP The post Aston Villa to take legal action against pundit Carragher appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Peter Obi Joins Seriake Dickson For Bayelsa Homecoming, Boat Regatta
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, travelled to Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, to attend the grand homecoming ceremony honouring Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, the National Leader of their party. The visit drew large crowds of supporters and provided a platform for Obi to outline alternative governance strategies, sharply contrasting current federal administrative practices with his own policy platform. Addressing stakeholders in the riverine state, Obi directed criticism toward President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s domestic presence and foreign travel record. “After more than three years in office, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has not considered it appropriate to spend even one night in Bayelsa State, despite spending over 260 days abroad,” Obi stated. Offering a direct commitment to regional engagement, he added: “I assured our numerous supporters and the people of Bayelsa State that this will not happen under my leadership. I will visit Bayelsa to hear directly from our people and respond to their concerns.” Peter Obi and Senator Henry Seriake Dickson taking part in a traditional boat regatta in Toru-Orua, Bayelsa State. (Photo credit: https://x.com/PeterObi) Pledging Regional Port Decentralisation Shifting focus to economic development, Obi addressed the maritime and commercial viability of the Niger Delta. Decrying the systemic underutilisation of coastal economic corridors, he committed to a decentralised port expansion strategy. “In Bayelsa, I pledged that we would begin efforts to upgrade ports throughout the Niger Delta, including those in Warri, Port Harcourt, and Calabar,” Obi announced. He further pledged to accelerate stalled regional projects: “We will also begin construction of the long-delayed Ibaka seaport in Akwa Ibom State and establish a new port in Bayelsa State to serve our riverine communities and the broader Niger Delta more effectively.” Obi reaffirmed his broader national policy framework, emphasising that national security, anti-corruption enforcement, and heavy capital investments in human capital—specifically healthcare and education—remain prerequisites for pulling citizens out of poverty. The political engagement concluded with traditional festivities as Obi joined Senator Henry Seriake Dickson in his hometown of Toru-Orua, situated within the Sagbama Local Government Area. Obi commended local and national party leadership for the coordination of the event, offering closing congratulations to his host: “I congratulate my dear brother, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, on his successful return home. item.title: Sowore reacts as Ekiti police arrest 11 over attack
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, Omoyele Sowore, and members of his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital. In a statement on Saturday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday, said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off. It partly reads, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti. “The suspects are Joseph Tayo ’32yrs’, Olatunji Abayomi ’41yrs’, Isaac Amba ’22yrs’, Kehinde Ajigbana ’18yrs’, Tosin David ’18yrs’, Solomon Iyanu ’18yrs’, Ogunsola Ayomide ’21yrs’, Ojo Ayodeji ’22yrs’, Kayode Dada ’32yrs’, Segun Olatunji ’28yrs’ and Salami Emmanuel ’53yrs’. “Items recovered include two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, one pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards, thirteen mobile phones, two vehicle keys, one flash drive, one 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, one gas lighter and ₦250.” The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the individual roles of the suspects and determine their possible connections with the attack. The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.” Reacting to the arrests, Sowore demanded that the alleged masterminds and sponsors of the attack be identified and brought to justice, insisting that the incident was a coordinated assault and not an ordinary altercation. The presidential candidate made the demand in a post on X on Saturday, describing the arrests as an admission that the incident was a violent attack. He also alleged that some of the attackers were associated with the City Boys group and called for investigations into possible links between the incident and officials of the state government. Sowore urged the Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, and the Department of State Services to preserve and release CCTV footage from the scene to help identify those involved. “Arresting 11 suspects is not enough if those who planned, financed, coordinated and facilitated the attack remain untouched,” he wrote. He also demanded an explanation from the police over their initial description of the incident as an altercation. item.title: Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
item.description: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website. The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them. Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February. According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response”. It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”. The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region. The supreme leader’s statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting. A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance. According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter. The post Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sanwo-Olu rallies LGs for cleanliness contest, insists on Lagos monthly sanitation
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni ​The Lagos State Government has unveiled plans to launch a state-wide cleanliness competition across all 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs) and 37 Local Council Development Areas (LCDAs), aimed at driving community-led environmental hygiene and recognizing the cleanest localities in the state. ​Wife of the Lagos State Governor, Dr. Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu announced the initiative on Saturday, during the monthly environmental sanitation monitoring exercise for the October in Ikorodu, marking the seventh monthly cleanup since the initiative resumed in March, where she also strongly defended the relevance of the monthly exercise against public criticism. Also, in a simultaneous event held in Ikeja Local Government Area, the Head of Service, Mr. Bode Agoro, issued a stern warning to residents against dumping waste into canals and drainage channels, cautioning that the illegal practice severely threatens public sanitation and heightens the risk of flash flooding across the state. Agoro was accompanied by the chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area, Akeem Olalekan Dauda, popularly called AKOD and other executive members of the council. ​Sanwo-Olu expressed satisfaction with the high level of community participation and environmental standard observed along major roads and commercial hubs in Ikorodu. ​”I am very impressed. I noticed that they have taken our environmental sanitation very seriously. While we were coming, I was looking at the cleanliness along the roads, especially in the market spaces,” Mrs Sanwo-Olu stated. ​Highlighting the early turnout of young residents, waste management crews, traffic officers, and traditional leaders, she added: “Importantly, we noticed our children; they had been here since 6:00 a.m. They had been cleaning even before I came.The LAWMA staff were also working, and the sweepers were outside. All hands were on deck.” ​Challenging Ikorodu residents to sustain the momentum and aim for top honours in the upcoming council-wide competition, Mrs Sanwo-Olu urged residents to embrace hygiene as a daily routine rather than a monthly obligation. ​”My message to them is that they should keep Lagos clean and not only wait till we have our environmental sanitation day. but make sure that Ikorodu comes first in the competition ahead. “All the local governments will take part, and they will announce the best or the cleanest environment in Lagos very soon,” she said. ​Addressing public debates questioning the necessity of the monthly sanitation exercise, the First Lady dismissed claims that the program wastes state resources. item.title: UK PM ‘open’ to slavery apology but not reparations
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations. The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean. “I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today,” Burnam wrote in the Guardian newspaper. The transatlantic slave trade was a “brutal and barbaric violation” of the rights of those enslaved, he said. The British premier added his government wanted a “structured dialogue with those affected”. “Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them.” The king is due to address the Commonwealth summit, which runs from November 1 to 4. Britain’s central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch’s Caribbean tour. In the Bahamas on Tuesday, Charles acknowledged “the great suffering of the past” during the first leg of his visit. Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations. Burnham again rejected financial compensation, writing: “I do not believe that is the right answer.” “I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part.” Britain profited for centuries from colonialism and the slave trade. In 1833, parliament passed a law to abolish slavery. Vanguard News The post UK PM ‘open’ to slavery apology but not reparations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: One killed, 6 wounded in US Halloween store shooting
item.description: A shooting at a Halloween store in northern California killed one person and wounded six on Friday, police said, adding investigators had not yet identified who was responsible. The incident occurred shortly before 8:30 pm (0330 GMT Saturday) at a Spirit Halloween store at a shopping mall in Fairfield, about 47 miles (76 kilometers) northeast of San Francisco. Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall told reporters one person was killed and six others were hospitalized with gunshot wounds. At least three were in critical condition, he added. “There is still a very active crime scene and investigation going on right now,” Marshall said late Friday, noting police had not yet identified the “suspect or suspects” responsible. The shooting took place hours before the start of Halloween, which is celebrated in the United States on Saturday. Marshall said no areas outside of the Solano Town Center mall were on lockdown. item.title: The Signal: INEC Draws The Line, The Politicians Must Now Face The Voters
item.description: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. The politicians are still negotiating power. The electoral commission is beginning to determine who can contest it. For weeks, Nigeria’s political conversation has revolved around familiar questions. Who is supporting President Bola Tinubu? Can Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi agree on a common strategy? How much influence does Nyesom Wike command? Which governor will deliver which state? Then, on Friday, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reminded everyone that there is another player in this election: the umpire. INEC announced the outcome of its review of complaints arising from the exclusion of governorship and state assembly candidates. Some politicians received welcome news. Others discovered that their appeals had failed. Among the most notable decisions, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami succeeded in his petition concerning the Gombe governorship election, although his candidacy remains subject to pending litigation. Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, was less fortunate. His petition was rejected. These decisions may appear to be administrative matters. They are not. They affect the choices available to voters, the calculations of political parties, and potentially the balance of power in important states. And they arrive at a moment when INEC is already facing intense scrutiny over the integrity of the voters’ register. The emerging question is no longer simply which politician has the strongest campaign organisation. It is whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions can apply the rules consistently, resolve disputes transparently and command public confidence when the votes are counted. Pantami gets a reprieve. Adebutu does not. INEC’s latest decisions offer a revealing picture of the difficulties political parties are experiencing with the Electoral Act and candidate nomination procedures. The commission received 69 petitions from 12 political parties across 26 states concerning governorship nominations. Of those, 41 succeeded, and 28 were rejected. For state assembly elections, 25 of the 61 petitions were successful, while 36 were rejected. The figures tell us something important. This is not an isolated disagreement involving one or two politicians. It is a substantial problem affecting party nominations across the country. The disputes concern membership registers, compliance with statutory deadlines, alleged multiple nominations and the wrongful inclusion or exclusion of candidates. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. But the pending court proceedings mean that the matter is not entirely settled

item.title: Iran’s army warns any new US attack would spread war wider
item.description: Iran’s army warned Saturday that any new US attack would only spread their war wider, following threats by America and Israel of further military action as they hold crucial elections. The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts underway to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US Vice President JD Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. “If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area,” Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said in a post on X, without elaborating. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also warned on Saturday that “Iran’s Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people”. On Friday, a Qatari delegation arrived in the Iranian capital for talks with senior Iranian officials. Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran’s security chief at the direction of President Donald Trump in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes. Iran has confirmed receiving the letter but has not announced any response. The US holds midterm elections on Tuesday that could determine the direction of the war, which has proven unpopular with American voters following a spike in energy prices due to the conflict. Last Tuesday, Israel also held legislative elections, with voters given a chance to offer a verdict on right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Under Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran’s government, Israel and Iran have engaged in direct military confrontations after decades of shadow war. The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that killed the country’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as well as senior military commanders. Iran in response targeted US assets across the Middle East as well as Israel. Most recently hostilities have focused on the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial Gulf shipping route for energy exports that Iran has blockaded since the start of the war. The US has in retaliation been blockading Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the nation’s economy. item.title: ONSA, DSS Rescue Three Zamfara Clerics Kidnapped En Route To Prayer Session For Tinubu
item.description: The Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) and the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, have rescued three Islamic clerics kidnapped while travelling to attend a special prayer session for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Zamfara State. The victims were among six Imams abducted on September 12, 2026, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them at about 11:30 a.m. along the Dakko-Damri feeder road, near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area, about three kilometres from Damri village, at Gidan Suleiman Bature. The clerics, identified among the group as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were reportedly travelling to Talata Mafara for a special prayer gathering seeking divine guidance and favour for President Tinubu’s administration and political future. Following the abduction, the kidnappers reportedly demanded a ransom of 30 million naira for their release. A senior security operative involved in the operation confirmed in Gusau that three of the clerics were rescued unharmed following a series of intelligence-led operations. The rescued clerics subsequently underwent medical examinations and security debriefings. They are said to be in stable condition and are expected to be formally handed over to the Zamfara State Government for reunification with their families. The clerics, identified among the group as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam The Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, CP Ahmad Muhammad Bello, also confirmed the successful operation, commending the collaboration among ONSA, the DSS and police operatives. Security agencies say operations are ongoing to track down the kidnappers and secure the release of the remaining three clerics still in captivity. They also called on members of the public to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information that could assist security operatives in identifying and apprehending criminal elements operating across the region. item.title: Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigerian Navy Marines at the Naval Base Lake Chad in conjunction with 403 Amphibious Brigade Nigerian Army, operating under Operation Hadin Kai, have recorded significant operational gains against Boko Haram Terrorists (BHT) in the Lake Chad area, neutralising 34 ISWAP/Boko Haram terrorists in the waters. Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, Director of Information while making this known on Saturday said the operation was conducted through intelligence-driven offensive. He said, “On 28 October 2026, the Nigerian Navy Marines conducted offensive operations against terrorist elements, with initial reports indicating that 8 terrorists were killed in action. “A subsequent Battle Damage Assessment revised the casualty figure to 28 terrorists killed in action. “In a separate operation on 30 October 2026, the Nigerian Navy Marines deployed at Naval Base Lake Chad conducted an offensive strike against identified Boko Haram terrorist enclave at Dumba. “The operation followed Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance missions that facilitated the identification and monitoring of terrorist elements before a precision strike was executed. “Preliminary Battle Damage Assessment indicates that approximately 6 terrorists were neutralised, while several others reportedly sustained injuries. “The casualty figures remain subject to further verification as operational assessments continue. “Since their deployment, the recently established Nigerian Navy Marines have served as a force multiplier under Operation Hadin Kai, strengthening the conduct of offensive operations against terrorist elements. “Their operational contributions have enhanced the capacity to target terrorist enclaves, disrupt hostile activities and deny Boko Haram Terrorists freedom of action within the Lake Chad area. “These efforts continue to support the degradation of terrorist capabilities and advance ongoing operations to restore peace and stability in the North East. “The Nigerian Navy remains committed to supporting joint operations through sustained offensive action and intelligence-driven engagements to strengthen national security and protect vulnerable communities.” The post Navy marines kill 34 terrorists, disrupt ISWAP/Boko Haram operations in Lake Chad appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senegal kicks off Youth Games, Africa’s first ever Olympics
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open Saturday in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “We’ve got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they’re going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar. “I think that is really important for our continent”, she said. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. – Sports culture – An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship. “Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth,” Senegal Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week. “Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it’s a symbol”, he said. – Russian athletes – With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee’s (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours. According to the ROC, 13 Russian athletes will participate and 10 coaches will accompany them to Senegal. “The kids are excited, it’s good news that our legitimate right to participate with the national anthem and Russian flag has been restored”, Anzor Gaunov, who coaches Anastasia Dobrovolskaya in judo, told AFP earlier this month in Moscow. item.title: ‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. item.title: Masussuka: Life, preaching, death
item.description: The murder of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, has stirred emotions and sparked conversations around the life and times of a popular preacher seen through different lenses. To his army of followers, he embodied peace, dignity and tolerance for religious differences. To his critics, he was a controversial scholar whose religious ideology and preaching were questionable. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, on Monday evening in front of his house at Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack claimed by the extremist group, Ansaru. Amnesty International has called on the Nigerian government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. Masussuka: We reject his ideology but condemn his killing – JIBWIS Imam Masussuka’s preaching, killing contrary to Islamic laws – Sheikh Maraya The 47-year-old cleric subscribed to and preached Quranic teachings, but, to greater extent, disregarded Hadith, the sayings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) – a stance that placed him at variance with his critics. He alleged that a lot of Hadiths being attributed to the Prophet were not from him, saying they were concocted by some people out of mischief. Masussuka reportedly began preaching at the tender age of 13 and rose to prominence with the advent of social media, through which he established himself as one of the most vocal clerics among the Qur’aniyun Islamic sect. Through his active social media platforms, his preaching gained more recognition, increasingly attracting attention from other sects with different ideologies. Masussuka’s increased visibility drew controversies around his ideology. One major controversy surrounding Masussuka’s teachings and ideology revolved around his rejection of certain Hadith traditions as authorities and forms of religious practice. According to other sects, his doctrine that only the Qur’an serves as the gateway to religious practice goes contrary to a larger belief that both the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet are central sources of Islamic guidance. Disagreements over his ideology became more pronounced and his teachings were challenged on several occasions. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Nigeria’s drug battle Investigations reveal that in states where the governors joined the APC only after winning elections, the process of integrating the party structure on ground has not been concluded, leading to suspicion between those who moved the governors and those they met on ground. In states like Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa and Kano, there are still vestiges of animosity between the two major camps of the defecting governors and those they met on ground. In states like Anambra and Osun, where the governors are members of other parties but have been integrated into the APC presidential campaign council, the preexisting party structures there have shown that they are not comfortable with the arrangement. States like Benue, Ondo, Katsina, Zamfara have shown that the contending forces are not aligned to work together for the reelection bid of its presidential candidate due to unrestrained rivalries between the governors and other powerful figures from the party in their states, who have the ears of Abuja. Our correspondents capture what is going on in some of the states. Masari yet to attend Radda’s campaign rallies in Katsina As the Katsina State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) begins its 2027 re-election campaign, the Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Political and Other Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, is yet to attend any of the party’s major campaign activities in the state. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections.
